item.title: GloRilla’s Sister Apologizes For Saying The Rapper Was Obligated To Share Her Wealth
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: GloRilla’s sister, BroRilla, is walking back her past comments about the Memphis rapper. The past year has been rocky between the sisters. A few months ago, BroRilla spoke with TMZ and aired out her issues with Glo, claiming that her sister wasn’t doing enough to take care of the family. “She got an obligation to […]
item.content:encoded:
GloRilla’s sister, BroRilla, is walking back her past comments about the Memphis rapper.

The past year has been rocky between the sisters. A few months ago, BroRilla spoke with TMZ and aired out her issues with Glo, claiming that her sister wasn’t doing enough to take care of the family.

“She got an obligation to share the wealth. We sat here and struggled together. Yea she obligated, them friends obligated? She doing everything for them. So I feel like I’m obligated. She not doing nothing for the family, at all.”

The FNF rapper later responded with receipts, sharing a FaceTime call with their parents that appeared to contradict BroRilla’s claims.

Fast-forward to now, and it looks like Big Glo’s sister is having a change of heart. BroRilla recently issued a public apology, admitting that her perspective has changed.

“I’m publicly apologizing to my sister. I’m sorry for feeling obligated. And the reason why I’m apologizing is because I’m going through what she could have went through.”

BroRilla went on to explain that she’s now making more money herself, giving her a better understanding of Glo’s position. However, she made it clear that there’s still a major difference between their bank accounts.

“Glo, I apologize because I’m in your shoes now. Well, I’m not in your shoes ‘cause you rich as a motherf*cker, you a millionaire, b*tch. I am a thousand-aire. Let’s not forget that.”

item.title: Duke Dennis & More Continue To Sound Off On ‘Hood Warfare 2’
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: Hood Warfare 2, a $5 gang-themed FPS, goes viral on Steam but faces backlash for glorifying Chicago gang violence and perpetuating harmful stereotypes.
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday, Trapstar Games’ Hood Warfare 2 had social media talking, and that continues to be the case as people continue to call out its glorification of Chicago’s gang violence.

For those who don’t know what the hell Hood Warfare 2 is, it’s a $5 Call of Duty clone that features the Bloods and Crips (we wish we were lying) battling out on Chicago’s streets. It is currently enjoying viral success after gameplay clips landed on social media.

The game is currently doing well on Steam and has a “mostly positive” rating based on 1,974 reviews.

Per the game’s Steam page, the description reads:

Rival gangs fight for control of Chicago. Pick a side, customize your weapons, and fight other players across a variety of action-packed game modes. Spin the block and take over the streets in this chaotic multiplayer FPS.

Hood Warfare 2 brings back the chaotic FPS gameplay and humor of the original, now built in Unreal Engine 5 with updated visuals, new weapon animations, and a new set of maps. Fight through downtown, the suburbs, The Trenches, and Chicago Mall. Hold down the streets or take the fight indoors, with different routes and positions to learn on each map.

Duke Dennis & Others Sound Off on Hood Warfare 2

The game has sparked plenty of chatter on social media, with some believing Hood Warfare 2 is some sort of CIA psyop to keep the Black community down.

The game was also discussed on a recent episode of the Joe Budden Podcast with co-host and gamer Ice, who felt a white person made it and that “it’s some secret hidden marketing” behind it.

AMP member Duke Dennis also shared his thoughts on the game, calling it out for its very stereotypical aspects.

“This game is so fcking cliche & predictable. Whoever made this game just couldn’t be black. If they was black, they either lack social awareness or they just don’t give a fck,” Dennis said during a stream.

RDC World felt the wrath of their chat and social media while streaming Hood Warfare 2.

Another thread is people trying to justify Hood Warfare 2’s existence by comparing it to games like Grand Theft Auto, 50 Cent: Bulletproof, and Saints Row.

But honestly, that is a huge stretch.

It’s going to be interesting as the conversation around Hood Warfare 2 continues, as people continue to push back on its blatant stereotypes and racism.

You can see more reactions below.

item.title: Lil Jon Recalls The Day His Son Passed Away In His New Book ‘I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me’
item.dc:creator: O Mazariego
item.description: Earlier this yer Lil Jon experienced a father’s worst nightmare when his 27-year-old son, Nathan Smith a.k.a. DJ Young Slade, tragically passed away in a drowning accident this past February. Now it seems like Lil Jon is ready to open up about the heartbreaking tragedy as People is reporting that in his new book, I […]
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this yer Lil Jon experienced a father’s worst nightmare when his 27-year-old son, Nathan Smith a.k.a. DJ Young Slade, tragically passed away in a drowning accident this past February.

Now it seems like Lil Jon is ready to open up about the heartbreaking tragedy as People is reporting that in his new book, I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me, Lil Jon writes about the last conversation he had with his son before he disappeared and was ultimately found days later. Telling People that he “needed to share everything I was going through,” Jon says that the book that he had been working on for years is now dedicated to the memory of his first-born son.

In an excerpt from his book, Lil Jon explained how his son was dealing with both mental stress and physical distress which led to Jon sending him to get “all kinds of tests” to see what kind of treatment he could get him in order to help him get better. Unfortunately it seems like it all became too much to bare for the young man as things took a horrible turn in February. Days after Nathan had gone missing, Lil Jon received a call from the police that they might’ve found his son’s body in a lake. Rushing to the scene, Jon had to endure the worst news any parent could ever receive about their child.

Per People:

The officer looked at me with a serious expression painted across his face. “I’m sorry to inform you, but we found your son.”

My head dropped. My heart broke. I was shell-shocked, overwhelmed with pain.

Just as nothing can prepare you for the moment your child enters the world, nothing can prepare you for the moment your child leaves the world.

Sobs filled the air. Then, quickly, I picked my head up and spoke with the officer more. People who were there told me later they felt like I held it together, all things considered. That while I was receiving the worst news of my life, I somehow kept my composure.

It was unthinkable, still. I knew Nathan was in indescribable physical discomfort, that it was debilitating. I knew he was also dealing with emotional pain. A lot of his pain stemmed from fear. That’s why I’d written those text messages after we talked a few days earlier. I hoped he could find relief from the pain and fear that was weighing on him so heavily.

Our hearts go out to Lil Jon and his family.

Though the family was heartbroken that Nathan had passed away, they found comfort in knowing the young man who felt the weight of the world on his shoulders was no longer having to deal with the mental anguish and physical struggles that had plagued him for so long.

The morning of the funeral, though, I woke up with a sense of peace in my heart, in my spirit, and in my soul. I later spoke to Nathan’s mother, and she reiterated the same thing: He is at peace now. His best friend told me he felt the same thing when he woke up that morning. Nathan was no longer in pain.

Lil Jon’s I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me is set to release on October 20th. Will you be checking the book out? Let us know in the comments section below.

item.title: Halle Berry’s Son Allowed To Testify In Custody Battle Amid Abuse Allegations
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez’s custody battle is getting messier, and now their teenage son could be called to testify in court. A judge has ruled that the former couple’s 13-year-old son, Maceo, can testify in the ongoing legal dispute following Martinez’s shocking allegations that Berry abused their child. “The minor child is permitted to […]
item.content:encoded:
Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez’s custody battle is getting messier, and now their teenage son could be called to testify in court.

A judge has ruled that the former couple’s 13-year-old son, Maceo, can testify in the ongoing legal dispute following Martinez’s shocking allegations that Berry abused their child.

“The minor child is permitted to testify,” Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Shelley Kaufman said in court documents obtained by the Daily Mail. However, the judge limited the testimony to “the request for the issuance of a restraining order.”

The ruling comes days after Martinez, 60, asked the court to allow Maceo to “address the court” and share his account of the alleged incident involving Berry, also 60, according to Page Six.

“Given that our son is 13 years old, I believe it would certainly be in his best interest for him to address the court at this time,” the French actor said in court documents.

“He should have the opportunity to have his voice heard regarding what he experienced that night,” Martinez added, arguing that their son’s testimony would be key to helping the court establish what happened on Sept. 26.

“I am the parent who wants the truth to come out. I am the parent who does not want to suppress Maceo’s voice,” he said.

Martinez has also asked the judge to block Berry’s daughter, Nahla Aubry, from testifying after the teenager reportedly defended her famous mother against the allegations.

“Ms. Aubry does not have any significant bearing on this case,” Martinez claimed in his filing, adding that she was “unquestionably biased.” He also argued that Berry should not involve her daughter in litigation that does not concern her.

Last month, Martinez filed for a temporary restraining order against Berry, accusing the Monster’s Ball actress of jumping on Maceo, putting her hands around his neck and choking him. Berry has vehemently denied the allegations.

The dispute has already affected the former couple’s custody arrangement. Martinez was granted primary custody of Maceo, while Berry was ordered to see their son two days a week and every other weekend.

Berry and Martinez married in 2013 and finalized their divorce in 2016. Now, nearly a decade after their marriage ended, their private family dispute is playing out in court, with their teenage son potentially caught in the middle.

item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’s Launch Trailer Features Crime, Shower Sex & A New Song Featuring SZA
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: Surprise, we got another look at Grand Theft Auto 6 ahead of its locked-in November 19 release date. Unlike the other trailers, there were no teases or indications this was coming, but here we are.
item.content:encoded:
While Cyberleek is still out here trying to spoil Grand Theft Auto 6 after his crypto scheme flopped, Rockstar Games dropped the launch trailer for the highly anticipated game, and it’s packed with new details.

Surprise, we got another look at Grand Theft Auto 6 ahead of its locked-in November 19 release date. Unlike the other trailers, there were no teases or indications this was coming, but here we are.

We Learn Jason’s Motives In Grand Theft Auto 6’s Launch Trailer

In the new trailer, which will likely air on television and before movies in theaters, further signaling that the game’s promotional machine is fully revved up, we quickly learn why Jason, one of the game’s protagonists, chose a life of crime.

 “I got in trouble in the army. Didn’t leave on the best of terms. They don’t give loans or anything to people like me,” Jason says in the 1:30 trailer.

The trailer also teases plenty of gunplay, car driving, crimes being committed, and, shockingly, steamy shower sex between Jason and his partner Lucia, further cementing that they are a couple and possibly teasing that this game will feature intimate moments that could put GTA V’s “hot coffee” mod to shame.

It was also hilarious to see Lucia still wearing her ankle monitor while Jason showers with her.

Like other GTA game trailers, this one also features music, a new song from the electronic duo Justice, who also scored Grand Theft Auto 6. The new track is called “Flower in a Hurricane,” and it features Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, and it will live on the companion album that will be dropped alongside the game.

The launch trailer follows a GamesBeat report claiming GTA 6 is coming to PC in the first quarter of 2027.

As you can imagine, the latest trailer only adds to the massive hype around this game. You can see those reactions below.

The legendary DJ brought out Baby Drill, Noodah05, Fatt Smaxk, Mykko Montana, and plenty more, giving the crowd a taste of Atlanta’s next wave of talent.

You haven’t truly experienced a homecoming concert until Jacquees hits the stage with “B.E.D.” When DJ Holiday brought out the King Of R&B, the crowd went wild, singing along word for word to his hits.

Que even had a surprise guest of his own, bringing out his artist Tyler Watts. The rising talent performed “Prettiest Girl,” a record that’s been making waves on TikTok.

item.title: Ava DuVernay Drops A Film Industry Hot Take: “Hollywood Is Over”
item.dc:creator: Keenan Higgins
item.description: Famed director Ava DuVernay made a bold comment about the state of the film industry amid current mergers and studio collapses in Hollywood.
item.content:encoded:
The film industry is going through a major shift at the moment as insiders and moviegoers alike try to make sense of the viral Paramount-Warner Bros. merger officially known as Skydance.

Famed director Ava DuVernay appeared on stage this past Monday (October 12) during the 70th BFI London Film Festival for a panel discussion centered on her latest documentary, 14th. In addition to giving some insight on her career path to date, she also made a bold statement regarding the current state of Hollywood.

Let’s just say DuVernay has a grave answer to what the mega-merger will mean for filmmaking.

RELATED: Little Known Black History Fact: Ava DuVernay’s 13th

The Billionaires Are Building Their Own Skynet. We’re Cooked

According to The Hollywood Reporter, DuVernay put an emphasis on crowdfunding during the Q&A session when asked how producers could finance films like hers, stating, “You put your movie up there, and there are all kinds of apps and sites that allow people who are like-minded to do it.” She went on to add, “But [it’s about] also just asking people, getting 20 people investing $5,000 — a nice amount of money to say something or make something. And there are ways to get that money back, whether it’s through taking the film around to different film festivals or YouTubing it or selling it. This is what we’re going back to.”

In highlighting how important alternate funding will be, the Emmy-winning filmmaker made her point clear by simply stating her hot take: “Hollywood is over.”

Doubling down on her point, she went on to tell the audience, “Did you guys hear?  It’s done. They’re buying each other, they’re collapsing. It’s all changed.  They’re selling studio lots. The idea of going to Sundance and getting a three-picture deal from Harvey Weinstein? He’s in prison.”

She summarized her point by noting that creatives will now more than ever have to rely on making direct connections to their audiences without the film studios acting as a middle man.

Although Netflix serves as the middle man when it comes to 14th, for DuVernay it’s about spreading the message as far as possible. The documentary gives historic context behind the 14 Amendment, and the current systematic attack against it regarding citizenship rights and equal protection under the law. In the same conversation, she spoke on the experience of making it by stating, “This film saved me in a lot of ways. … The rage that I feel and the fear that I feel, I was really being able to pour it into 14th every day. I only finished the film two weeks ago, and so I really don’t know what I’m going to do from here.”

We don’t think anyone wants to see Hollywood come to a full stop, but her point was made in making note of the power in shifting towards a DIY approach. With the rise of Skydance and a new generation questioning their place in the game, these are the conversations that will shape the future of filmmaking.

item.title: Social Media Believes $5 ‘Call of Duty’ Clone, ‘Hood Warfare 2’ Was Planted By The CIA
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: Hood Warfare 2, a $5 gang-based FPS game, went viral on social media but sparked controversy over its problematic subject matter and allegations of CIA involvement.
item.content:encoded:
A $5 Call of Duty-style FPS game where the Bloods and Crips fight over territory in Chicago? If you’re wondering whether this is a real game, yes, it is, and it’s currently gone viral on social media.

The game, which costs only the price of four chicken wings from the hood Chinese restaurant, is currently on Steam with very positive reviews and follows the original game, which peaked at 68 players when it first dropped.

Now, thanks to social media, Hood Warfare 2 from developer Trapstar Games is enjoying the success the first title missed out on.

The official synopsis for the game reads:

‘Rival gangs fight for control of Chicago. Pick a side, customize your weapons, and fight other players across a variety of action-packed game modes. Spin the block and take over the streets in this chaotic multiplayer FPS.

Hood Warfare 2 brings back the chaotic FPS gameplay and humor of the original, now built in Unreal Engine 5 with updated visuals, new weapon animations, and a new set of maps. Fight through downtown, the suburbs, The Trenches, and Chicago Mall. Hold down the streets or take the fight indoors, with different routes and positions to learn on each map.

Weapon customization gets an upgrade, too. Change out sights, magazines, grips, suppressors, and other attachments to get your gun how you want it. Set up your loadout with perks and equipment before heading into a match.’

Like the first game, the player count started out slow, but quickly ballooned as people like the folks from RDC World streamed it.

Social Media Believes Hood Warfare 2 Was Planted By The CIA

But it shouldn’t come as a surprise that a game based on such a problematic subject is sparking outrage, with a lot of critics calling out the fact that the game features Black gang members trying to kill each other in a game allegedly created by a white developer using AI.

Other complaints claim the game was somehow planted by the CIA and is nothing but a tool to keep Black folks down.

We’re not gonna hold you to it, but this game looks like a hot mess and isn’t worth $5. But it appears that’s not stopping people from playing it.

You can see more reactions to Hood Warfare 2 below.

Coi Leray woke up today and decided to let the world know where she stands when it comes to her relationship status.

It appears the New Jersey rapper’s highly publicized relationship with blogger Justin Laboy may be over, at least from her perspective.

“Single and not looking for anything. This world is just too cold.”

Leray and Laboy first sparked dating rumors in 2025 after rans noticed their chemistry during an interview. Following her appearance on his podcast, the two appeared to spend more time together, eventually confirming their relationship and going public.

There has been no confirmation of what may have led to a potential breakup. However, following her initial post, Leray shared another message that hinted at what she may be going through.

“Feel like I been in constant mode my whole life. This next chapter is personal.”

Laboy also appeared to respond indirectly to Leray’s declaration of being single, suggesting that there may be more to the situation than meets the eye.

“She’s definitely gonna get one of y’all shot she is not single.”

Neither has publicly clarified the situation, leaving fans to speculate about what may have happened between the two.

item.title: Urban One Enters Microseries Market With Thrillers ‘Power & Influence’ and ‘Foul Play’
item.dc:creator: Keenan Higgins
item.description: Urban One launches two original vertical microseries on TikTok optimized for mobile viewing, expanding entertainment into the growing digital streaming market.
item.content:encoded:
The world of entertainment is growing to match the times, particularly with digital streaming changing how we watch and enjoy our favorite shows. With the convenience of viewing straight from a phone screen paired with the new trend of clip sharing on social media, a new market in the industry developed with the rise of the microseries.

Urban One was clever enough to get in on the action with the announcement of two original vertical microseries created for mobile viewing to air on BOSSIP’s TikTok.

RELATED: True Crime Podcast Infamy, Joins Urban One’s Podcast Network

Both Power & Influence (seen above) and Foul Play will each include 20 episodes that average 90 seconds and expected to extend across Urban One’s multiplatform media ecosystem following its TikTok premiere. Power & Influence kicks things off beginning October 19 with a corporate thriller plot driven by AI deepfakes exposing hidden scandals at one of Atlanta’s most respected Black-owned advertising agencies. The cast includes Ivory Shields (Queen Sugar), Tanazia Madan (Nappily Ever After), Jay Jones (Lovecraft Country), De’Tuan Williams (Fear Lake Lanier), Ashley Brittney Silva (Love & Marriage: DC), Donny Carrington (Beyond the Gates). The series comes from the combined creativity of writer by Dreux Dougall of Lovecraft Country fame, director Jamal Simmons from Married at First Sight) and executive producer Ma’at Zachary.

Women’s basketball revenge thriller Foul Play is currently in production, bringing to life the directorial debut of former professional women’s basketball player and assistant coach, Ty Young. The series centers on a highly skilled military veteran and sports mom who seeks retribution against the corrupt coach, referee and player who conspired to injure her star point-guard daughter during a high-stakes tournament. Tanya Hoffler-Moore (Tyler Perry’s House of Payne) will write and executive produce, with co-direction and and co-production from Leon Lozano (All American: Homecoming) and women’s basketball players Ashley MacCalla and Sydney MacCalla.

“These microseries give brands an opportunity to connect authentically with our audiences through stories rooted in their culture and interests,” said Jeff Meza, Urban One’s EVP, Head of Branded Entertainment & Integrated Marketing. He also adds, “Partners can become part of those stories from the outset, with opportunities that extend across Urban One platforms.” That plan will include editorial support across iONE Digital properties like Hip-Hop Wired and MadameNoire, versions adapted for TV One, connected TV and free ad-supported streaming channels, plus promotion across Radio One stations, REACH Media syndicated shows and the Urban One Podcast Network.

Get the popcorn ready, and make sure to charge up your mobile devices!

item.title: The Top 25 Most Pest-Infested Cities in America
item.dc:creator: Nick Cottongim
item.description: Los Angeles tops the list of America's most pest-infested cities, followed by Chicago and Washington D.C. Regional patterns show Midwest and Northeast cities struggle with bed bugs and rodents, while Southern cities battle termites and mosquitoes.
item.content:encoded:
The Top 25 Most Pest-Infested Cities in America

Nobody wants to share their home with uninvited guests, but in some American cities, the bugs and critters have practically signed the lease. A new ranking from PestControlPricing.com combines Orkin’s 2025 top-50 lists for bed bugs, rodents, mosquitoes and termites into a single score.

A perfect 200 would mean a city topped all four lists. Los Angeles comes in at No. 1 with a near-perfect 196, leading the nation in both rodents and mosquitoes. Chicago follows close behind as the bed bug capital of the country, and Washington, D.C. rounds out the top three.

And yes, Indianapolis made the cut, landing at No. 10 overall, mostly because it ranks No. 5 for bed bugs.

Cities in the Midwest and Northeast tend to struggle most with bed bugs and rats, while Southern cities fight termites and mosquitoes.

Here’s the full list of the 25 most pest-infested cities in America, ranked by composite score.

RELATED | Craziest Haunted House Attractions In America

RELATED | 2026 Best Small Cities in America

1. Los Angeles, CA (196/200)

America’s top city for both rats and mosquitoes, and the mosquito capital four years running. It also ranks #2 for termites and #4 for bed bugs. Warm weather, a dense population and standing water keep pests active all year.

item.title: Sergio Hudson Is Giving The OshKosh Classics We Grew Up Loving A High-Fashion Makeover With A Little Help From His Godson
item.dc:creator: Lauren E. Williams
item.description: Designer Sergio Hudson launches his first kidswear collection with Carter's OshKosh, bringing his signature style to classic playground clothes inspired by his godson.
item.content:encoded:
Sergio Hudson is taking his signature fashion designs from the runway to the playground with his first-ever kidswear line. And the inspiration behind the capsule is someone very special to him: his godson Croi.

“Most of it was inspired by my godson Croix, who’s actually in one of the pictures and in the ad campaign,” Sergio told HelloBeautiful exclusively about his new collaboration with Carter’s OshKosh and Harlem’s Fashion Row.

He smiled as he shared that Croix has been picking out his own clothes since he was about 2 years old.

Sergio’s newest collaboration comes as his namesake brand celebrates 10 years and stays in celebrity rotation. Last month, Sergio presented his Spring/Summer 2027 collection at NYFW, inspired by his version of the Bond girl. Everything we know and love about Sergio Hudson’s designs came down the runway: bright monochromatic looks, sophisticated silhouettes, powerful feminine designs and impeccable tailoring.

After revisiting his fashion classics and turning them on their heads, Sergio is putting his spin on another American classic: OshKosh. So, you already know these aren’t your average playground clothes.

I’ve covered Sergio for years, attended his NYFW shows, and even explored his Volvo fashion collaboration up close. But this was my first time seeing him design for the little ones.

OshKosh and Harlem’s Fashion Row invited me to an exclusive preview of the collection during Carter’s holiday showcase. And as someone who absolutely loves Christmas, the October event had me smiling. We’re talking Christmas trees, snowflakes, wrapped gifts and holiday mocktails.

But the best gift of the afternoon? Getting an up-close look at Sergio’s new collection.

Sergio Hudson Gives OshKosh The Fashion Treatment

As an ’80s baby, I remember when OshKosh overalls were the thing. Wearing them to the playground, school or wherever your parents took you meant you were one of the best-dressed kids on the block. Even before we knew what “best dressed” was.

Sergio remembers, too.

“This is iconic as like a Ralph Lauren to me,” he said, explaining why the collaboration was an immediate yes.

He revisited classic denim jackets, overalls, tracksuits and hickory stripes, adding his signature saturated colors and matching pieces. “I kind of Sergio-tized it,” he joked.

He also personalized the buttons, labels and stripes with both brands’ names. His famous monochromatic approach made it into the collection, too.

“I love a monochromatic moment,” he told me. Sergio continued, saying, “[the collection] has great pieces that you can include in your children’s wardrobe and mix it up, which is what I do with my line.”

His Godson Croi And Two Daughters Helped Shape The Collection

“I feel like a kid should look like a kid,” he explained as he discussed kids dressing their ages. His two daughters, ages 13 and 15, also influenced his thinking. “I put a hoodie in the collection for them because that’s all they wear,” he joked.

Croix, meanwhile, even selected his own outfits during the campaign shoot. Sergio loved watching him make the clothes his own.

The limited-edition OshKosh x Sergio Hudson collection arrives October 22 at select stores and carters.com. In addition to the hoodies, pieces include aviator jackets, trainsuits, and, of course, overalls. Sizes range from 12 months to 14 years, with prices from $22 to $45.

Sergio has dressed some of our favorite women, and his next chapter includes a much younger fashion crowd.

Something tells me the coolest kid on the playground might be wearing Sergio Hudson.

item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami stopped by The Morning Hustle ahead of her album Watch Dis, which drops October 23rd, and she came ready. On the music side, Yung Miami released two singles at once, “F You” and “2008,” to be “disruptive.” She calls “2008” a hood record inspired by Jeezy, the Snowman she grew up listening to in Miami.

She confirmed that she and Kodak Black apologized to each other and moved past their old issues. Lil Baby, Quavo, and the Quality Control camp? She calls them family.

When it comes to Caresha balancing work with health, she say now she works out five days a week. She also uses a meal prep service offered through her gym to stay on track while she works. Studio sessions happen mostly in Atlanta, away from home distractions. Her formula is a nap first, dark lights, and recording completely solo. “My energy gotta be good,” she explained, because that energy shows up on the record.

Her adult drinking card game, Resha Roulette, grew out of her love for hosting game nights. Fair warning: some cards are strictly for grown folks.

She also addressed Lisa Raye’s viral criticism of “Spend Dat,” a song whose video pays homage to The Players Club. She also admitted she reads her comments, including Twitter trolls telling her to “get a CDL,” the meme urging women rappers to quit music and drive trucks. Miami doesn’t seemed concerned with naysayers as she awaits for her debut solo album.

Chanchez said he is in the best stage of his life. He described knowing himself, feeling whole and co-creating his life with the Creator. He shares more with Malik […]
item.content:encoded:
Hosea Chanchez joined The Morning Hustle to celebrate 20 years of The Game. The conversation covered his famous role, his health, his business and his past. Chanchez said he is in the best stage of his life. He described knowing himself, feeling whole and co-creating his life with the Creator.


He shares more with Malik Wright than many fans realize. Both were raised by single mothers in homes, but in real life his grandmother served as the matriarch, which gave him a sibling-like bond with his mom. Chanchez revealed he first auditioned and tested for Derwin Davis before landing Malik months later. The cast built a close bond as the show moved from UPN to The CW.

He also addressed dating rumors, confirming he never dated Tamera Mowry, the sister of his co-star Tia Mowry. He opened up also about Malik giving him an outlet. He grew up surrounded by supportive Black women, and the role’s macho confidence, modeled after Deion Sanders and Terrell Owens, let him release everyday micro aggressions.

Off screen, he announced his company, A Very Good Company. It is home to The Dawn of Good, a skincare line for men of color, and Good and Co, an upcoming wellness platform. Chanchez shared that he struggled with low testosterone after turning 40, including brain fog and fatigue. He said testosterone replacement therapy changed his life.

item.title: She’s Definitely Not Like Us: Senator Marsha Blackburn Dragged For Cringe Kendrick Lamar AI-Slop Video
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: GOP Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who is currently running for Governor of Tennessee, is being swamped with well-deserved backlash after she shared AI-generated slop featuring herself as Kendrick Lamar performing his iconic Drake diss, "Not Like Us," flanked by Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.), Sen. Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), state Sen. Brent Taylor, and Glenn Thomas Jacobs, the former WWE wrestler known as Kane.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans don’t hide the fact that they love to make the lives of Black people absolutely miserable, but they sure as hell love our contributions to entertainment.

GOP Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who is currently running for Governor of Tennessee, is being swamped with well-deserved backlash after she shared AI-generated slop featuring herself as Kendrick Lamar performing his iconic Drake diss, “Not Like Us,” flanked by Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.), Sen. Bill Hagerty (R-Tenn.), state Sen. Brent Taylor, and Glenn Thomas Jacobs, the former WWE wrestler known as Kane.

What makes this even more ridiculous is that Republicans were big mad about Lamar’s very politically charged performance, calling it “Satanic,” “absolute trash,” and other ridiculous statements because the Compton native dared to use the big stage to send a message.

Social Media Drags Marsha Blackburn

Social media wasted no time clowning Blackburn and calling her out for using Lamar’s moment, knowing she couldn’t care less about him or his message.

“DELETE THIS NOW! You don’t even like Black people,” one reply to Blackburn’s post read.

Another post read, “Colonizers make me sick. They hate Black culture but then wanna use to seem cool. Go to hell nest head.”

“This woman out here exploiting Black culture to run for governor in a state that passed a map eliminating the only majority Black district and weaken Black residents voting power. Fucking disgusting,” another user said.

Blackburn’s blatant misuse of Lamar’s moment is on par with MAGA Republicans’ behavior regarding pop culture. Donald Trump and his current administration are absolutely notorious for doing the same, using popular songs, video games, and other media, knowing the people involved don’t want anything to do with him.

We truly hope Blackburn gets her butt handed to her in the upcoming election.

You can see more reactions to her using Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us” below.

item.title: 15 B-Sides Showing D’Angelo At His Most Soulful
item.dc:creator: paige.boyd
item.description: Explore the legacy of D'Angelo with 15 B-Sides that are purely soulful, authentic, and unapologetically Black.
item.content:encoded:
When you think of the so-called “Neo Soul” movement, few names are held in as much reverence as D’Angelo.

Breaking through the music scene in the mid-1990s, D’Angelo blended classic R&B sounds with Hip-Hop influence. The method to his madness was rather simplistic in nature. In a 2014 conversation with longtime friend/collaborator Questlove (captured by The Guardian), the musician was authentically pure. “It’s about capturing the spirit, capturing that vibe,” he said. “I’m a first-take kinda dude.”

He also politely pushed back on the Neo Soul label. What he said next best summarized how his legacy would be remembered.

“I don’t want to disassociate, and I respect it for what it is, but any time you put a name on something, you put it in a box. I never claimed I do neo soul. When I first came out, I said, I do black music.”

With that said, here are 15 B-Sides of D’Angelo’s that are soulful, riveting, and, yes, unapologetically Black.

item.title: ‘The Oval’ Actor Travis Cure Sued By Ex Who Claims He Gave Her Herpes
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: The Oval star Travis Cure is at the center of a messy lawsuit filed by his former situationship, who is accusing the actor of giving her an incurable STD. Cure claims that he does have said STD but always wore a condom when having sex with his ex. Because apparently, what happens in the situationship […]
item.content:encoded:
The Oval star Travis Cure is at the center of a messy lawsuit filed by his former situationship, who is accusing the actor of giving her an incurable STD. Cure claims that he does have said STD but always wore a condom when having sex with his ex. Because apparently, what happens in the situationship doesn’t always stay in the situationship.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Cure’s former partner claims that the two started dating around August 2024. The woman said that while the two may not have been exclusive, she was not sleeping with anyone other than Travis from August 2024 until she filed her lawsuit.

She claims that Travis knew he had genital herpes but never disclosed his diagnosis before they had sex. She is accusing the actor of negligence and battery, arguing that he failed to inform her of a sexually transmitted infection that could have lasting consequences for her health.

In response to the lawsuit, Travis noted that the woman suing him said that they were not “exclusive on either side.” Cure added that the woman lives in Chicago and was having sex with other men while they were dating. Apparently, this situationship came with a whole lot of fine print about what each person was doing when they weren’t together.

Cure claims that he knew he had herpes and that the woman who filed the lawsuit also knew about his diagnosis. In his response, he suggested that the STD issue only became a point of contention after he ended things with her and found himself a girlfriend. Nothing says an old situationship is officially over quite like a lawsuit, apparently.

He also argued that there was no way for his ex to prove he gave her herpes, pointing to what he described as her “promiscuous sexual practices.” In other words, Cure is disputing that he was responsible for transmitting the infection and is challenging the woman’s ability to establish that claim.

Of course, having herpes and proving who transmitted it are two separate issues. Genital herpes is a lifelong viral infection, and condoms can reduce the risk of transmission but do not eliminate it entirely. Whether the woman’s claims hold up in court is another matter.

For now, the former couple’s private bedroom business has become a public legal battle, with both sides offering very different accounts of what the other knew and when they knew it.

The case is ongoing.

First, Interscope Records reportedly sued the R&B singer for more than $5 million, claiming she owes the label that amount. Now, Walker is turning her attention to LVRN, seeking legal action against the label, according to reports. The Atlanta-based singer is accusing […]
item.content:encoded:
Summer Walker has been dealing with multiple legal battles surrounding her record deals.

First, Interscope Records reportedly sued the R&B singer for more than $5 million, claiming she owes the label that amount. Now, Walker is turning her attention to LVRN, seeking legal action against the label, according to reports.

The Atlanta-based singer is accusing Love Renaissance Records of fraudulently withholding money and abusing the control it has over her as an artist. Walker signed with LVRN when she was 19 years old. In a 10page complaint, she alleges that the label failed to properly distribute funds from her budget and concealed revenue generated through platforms using her name.

“The LVRN Agreement granted particularly oppressive and extensive rights to defendant, and controlling influence over Walker.”

The complaint also alleges that LVRN sold merchandise featuring Walker’s name and likeness on Amazon without compensating her. Additionally, she claims the label improperly managed her YouTube page, allegedly deleting historical data she considers vital.

Walker is now asking the court to terminate her contract with LVRN and award her compensatory and punitive damages over the alleged contractual breaches.

As the legal dispute unfolds, more details could emerge about Walker’s efforts to separate herself from the label.

item.title: Keffe D Sentenced To 40 Years To Life In Prison For Tupac Shakur’s Murder
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the lone person charged in the shooting death of Tupac Shakur, has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison, Tuesday. Davis was facing the possibility of life without parole. The conviction comes just 30 years after the beloved rapper was gunned down in a drive-by shooting near the Las […]
item.content:encoded:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the lone person charged in the shooting death of Tupac Shakur, has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison, Tuesday. Davis was facing the possibility of life without parole. 

The conviction comes just 30 years after the beloved rapper was gunned down in a drive-by shooting near the Las Vegas Strip on Sept. 7, 1996. Shakur was rushed to a nearby hospital where he died six days later, TMZ reports.

For years, Davis had been suspected and questioned in the killing, but there was never enough evidence for prosecutors to bring charges. As time went on Davis became comfortable telling his account of what happened the night that Shakur was killed, even going so far as recounting moments from the shooting and describing himself as the  “shot caller” role in the infamous killing. Prosecutors allege that he helped organize the drive-by shooting and even supplied the .40 glock that was used to take Shakur’s life.

“I beat the streets, I beat the Feds, and I beat cancer,” prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo quoted Davis’ own words to the jury in his closing argument. “Now, he’s trying to beat 12 of you… Mr. Davis is attempting to escape responsibility for a crime everybody knows he committed, even him… End of the day, hold him accountable for the crime he committed.”

From his own account, Davis, 63, was a Los Angeles gang leader who would leave the gang life behind for the Vegas suburbs. Davis was arrested in September 2023 and charged with “murder with the use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang, in connection with Shakur’s murder,” CBS News reports. 

He’s been in custody since his arrest and pleaded not guilty to all charges. Davis’ lawyers argued the former gang leader lied about his involvement and that there was no proof that he was in Vegas on the night Shakur was killed.  

“The danger in this case has always been, just because we say something, is it true?” Davis’ lawyer Michael Sanft said.

Davis, 63, has already noted that he plans to appeal the conviction.

item.title: Netflix Is Bringing Young Thug’s YSL RICO Trial To The Screen In New Documentary
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: Netflix is bringing Young Thug’s infamous YSL RICO trial to our living rooms with a new documentary that will take viewers inside one of Hip-Hop’s most talked-about legal cases. The highly publicized trial captivated audiences as prosecutors attempted to prove that Young Thug’s record label, YSL, was a criminal street gang. Now, Netflix has gathered […]
item.content:encoded:
Netflix is bringing Young Thug’s infamous YSL RICO trial to our living rooms with a new documentary that will take viewers inside one of Hip-Hop’s most talked-about legal cases.

The highly publicized trial captivated audiences as prosecutors attempted to prove that Young Thug’s record label, YSL, was a criminal street gang. Now, Netflix has gathered footage from the proceedings for a 90-minute documentary titled Young Thug On Trial.

Fans can expect in-depth look at the twists and turns of the case, from the courtroom  drama to the moments that ultimately led to Thugger’s release. In 2024, the Atlanta rapper pleaded guilty to multiple charged and received a sentence that includes 15 years of probation.

“Major feature documentary covering the extraordinary rise and trial of Jeffery Williams, aka Young Thug, and his band of brothers from the streets of Atlanta,” the Netflix description reads. “Prosecutors set out to prove that he and his music label were actually a criminal street gang. High drama meets farce in this incredible story where a city and even rap itself are on trial.”

While Netflix has yet to announce an official release date, the documentary is expected to arrive in 2027.

This also isn’t Netflix’s first time taking a deep dive into the world Hip-Hop. In 2022, the streaming platform released jeen-yuhs: A Kanye Trilogy, chronicling Kanye West’s rise to fame. More recently, 50 Cent executive-produced a Netflix documentary centered on the allegations and legal troubles surrounding Diddy.

With Young Thug On Trial on the way, viewers will soon get another look at a case that had the entire Hip-Hop community watching as it unfolded.

item.title: Apple Announces Lineup Of New Smart Home Devices
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: Apple launches its new Home Collection smart home accessories, partnering with LG and Schneider Electric to compete with Google in the home automation market.
item.content:encoded:
Apple fanatics, this news is for you. You already have everything Apple, including your MacBook, iPhone, iPad, AirPods, HomePod, and Apple TV. Still, now the tech giant wants to take over your home, literally, with its new lineup of smart home accessories, the Apple Home Collection, in partnership with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

That’s right, you no longer need to rely on Google or other companies to turn your digs into a smart home; Apple has officially entered that space.

The company Steve Jobs built dabbled in the home space with devices like the HomePod speaker, but it’s now expanding that lineup with the new Home Collection.

Apple’s revamped Home Collection now includes the HomeView hub, HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K.

So let’s break it all down.

The Apple HomeView

The HomeView features a seven-inch Liquid Retina Display with a built-in speaker mount and can sit on your kitchen counter, in your living room, or be wall-mounted.

The HomeView costs $299, serves as the hub for your Apple-powered smart home, and lets you access your other devices.

According to Apple, HomeView can recognize up to six household members via facial recognition, giving each person access to their own apps, notifications, and more. Like your iPhone, iPad, or MacBook, HomeView can also play music, your favorite podcasts, FaceTime calls, or videos to help you in the kitchen.

Through HomeView, users can also control lights, smart locks, and thermostats; check and edit calendars; interact with Siri AI; and locate lost items like keys or wallets, provided they have an Apple AirTag attached.

It officially goes on sale Nov.13.

The Apple Home Collection

In the home space, Apple has taken a backseat to Google, but that’s changing under newly minted CEO John Ternus, who recently took control after Tim Cook stepped down.

With the Home Collection, the tech giant is looking to dominate a new space, with help from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

The Apple Home Collection features an LG in-home camera that can monitor your home and, for privacy, you can tell it to face down.

An outdoor camera monitors the outside, like deliveries, and recognizes familiar faces.

An LG door camera and lock can unlock when it recognizes your iPhone as you get close, quickly granting you access to your home.

Apple says setting up these devices is as seamless as setting up a pair of AirPods, giving fans of the brand smart home products that they will love while boasting elite privacy protection features.

But that’s not all that was announced. Apple also unveiled the $149 HomePod mini 2, featuring Siri AI integration and new colors.

It’s not just for enjoying iTunes or whatever DSP you stream from; you can also add events to your calendar or ask it questions.

Apple TV 4K Introduces A Much Better Experience

Apple TV 4K completes the new smart home collection at $299 and features built-in far-field microphones that let you issue commands to the set-top box instead of holding down the remote’s microphone button.

Apple TV 4K is available for pre-order starting today and will be available on Nov.13.
